question: What is the primary public health goal of Post-Abortion Care services?

options.B: Eliminating the incidence of ectopic pregnancy

explanation: PAC aims directly at treating complications of unsafe or spontaneous abortions to lower maternal death and illness rates. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h1)

question: Why must family planning services be integrated directly into post-abortion care?

options.A: To ensure immediate return to fertility and prevent rapid repeat unintended pregnancies
options.B: To fulfill mandatory national health insurance requirements for female patients
options.C: To permanently suppress ovarian function until elective marriage occurs
options.D: To diagnose underlying congenital uterine anomalies before discharge

explanation: Fertility returns very quickly following an abortion, making immediate contraceptive counseling essential for preventing another unintended pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h1)

question: Which component is officially recognized as one of the five essential elements of comprehensive PAC?
explanation: Treating incomplete abortion and associated injuries is a foundational medical element of the PAC framework. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of community engagement within the framework of post-abortion care?

options.A: Enforcing local bylaws regarding traditional herbal abortifacients
options.B: Replacing professional clinic staff with trained community volunteers
options.C: Ensuring timely recognition of danger signs and prompt referral to health facilities
options.D: Conducting mandatory household audits on fertility rates

explanation: Community engagement bridges the gap between grassroots populations and health facilities, ensuring women reach care before life-threatening complications escalate. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h2)

question: What is the preferred surgical method for managing a first-trimester incomplete abortion in resource-limited settings?
explanation: Manual Vacuum Aspiration is fast, safe, and cost-effective for clearing retained products in the first trimester without heavy anesthesia. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h3)

question: A patient is admitted with a diagnosis of incomplete abortion and signs of acute pelvic sepsis. What immediate nursing action should be prioritized before uterine evacuation?

options.A: Discharging the patient with oral analgesics for home care management
options.B: Initiating broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics and fluid resuscitation
options.C: Administering high-dose combined oral contraceptive pills
options.D: Scheduling an elective magnetic resonance imaging scan of the pelvis

explanation: Stabilizing the patient with fluids and fighting infection with antibiotics is vital before undertaking uterine evacuation to prevent septic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h3)

question: How soon can ovulation typically resume following an incomplete or complete abortion?
explanation: The ovarian cycle restarts rapidly after pregnancy termination, making early contraceptive initiation essential. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h4)

question: What standard must guide a nurse when offering family planning counseling to a post-abortion client?

options.A: Client-centered, voluntary, and free from provider bias
options.B: Strictly limited to barrier methods for religious reasons
options.C: Mandated use of long-acting permanent sterilization

explanation: Ethical nursing care requires respecting patient autonomy, offering full information without imposing personal beliefs. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h4)

question: Why is intentional psychosocial support vital during post-abortion care?

options.A: Patients often experience complex emotional responses including stigma, guilt, or trauma
options.B: Emotional support prevents future physical infections permanently
options.C: Psychological counseling replaces the need for surgical evaluation
options.D: Mental health assessments are legally required to prescribe antibiotics

explanation: Abortion experiences can evoke heavy emotional distress that requires compassionate nursing intervention and a safe clinical space. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate psychological nursing intervention for a distressed PAC client?

options.A: Providing a confidential and private environment
options.B: Scolding the client for engaging in unsafe practices

explanation: Scolding or judgmental behavior breaches professional ethics and worsens patient trauma, whereas the other options are supportive. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h5)

question: What is a major consequence of social stigma and legal restrictions regarding abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of low-cost surgical supplies
options.B: Immediate hospital admission for all elective procedures
options.C: Women seeking clandestine care from unqualified practitioners
options.D: A complete absence of spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: Stigma and fear drive women underground, leading to unsafe procedures performed by unqualified individuals and high complication rates. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h6)

question: How can nurses actively help overcome access barriers to post-abortion care in local communities?

options.A: Restricting PAC treatment strictly to married women with proof of marriage
options.B: Reporting all patients presenting with complications to law enforcement
options.C: Charging high informal fees to deter repeat visits
options.D: Providing confidential, non-judgmental care and building referral linkages

explanation: Creating a welcoming, confidential, and accessible healthcare environment encourages women to seek timely professional help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h6)

question: What is a primary purpose of tracking clinical indicators in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: Punishing healthcare workers for low patient turnover
options.B: Identifying gaps in service delivery to guide quality improvement
options.C: Eliminating the need for medical record keeping
options.D: Increasing the financial cost of hospital admissions

explanation: Monitoring metrics helps management spot clinical and logistical weaknesses so care quality can be systematically upgraded. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h7)

question: Which indicator is most critical to evaluate the success of post-abortion contraceptive counseling?

options.A: Frequency of routine facility cleaning schedules
options.B: Contraceptive acceptance rate prior to facility discharge
options.C: Average length of patient hospital stay in days
options.D: Total number of surgical evacuations performed monthly

explanation: Measuring how many clients adopt a method before leaving indicates how effectively counseling translates into preventive action. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h7)
